data.narrative:
Ocius Technology, a Series B-stage defense and security company founded by Robert Dane, is evaluated against a comp universe of 10 peers (2 public, 8 private) operating in the same sector and stage. The company has raised A$176M through an Australian Program of Record contract as of March 2026.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $176M capital base as a proxy and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical for Series B advancement, implying a $334M valuation. Peer-median analysis examines seven same-sector, same-stage comparables—including Dream Security ($3.0B), Harmattan AI ($1.4B), Code Metal ($1.2B), Castelion ($1.0B), and Defense Unicorns ($1.0B)—establishing a median of $1.0B with a range spanning $300M to $3.0B.

The triangulated analysis produces a valuation range of $284M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $667M. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around peer selection and the applicability of stage-progression mechanics to a capital-backed, contract-stage company. Key drivers of the range include variability in comparable company maturity and revenue profiles within the defense sector, as well as the atypical funding structure via government contract rather than conventional venture capital. Tighter conviction would require visibility into Ocius's revenue run-rate and customer concentration metrics relative to named peers.
